newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end slightly firmer, platinums up.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end slightly firmer, platinums up.

text.p: South African shares ended slightly firm after retracing early losses sparked by some profit-taking but Amplat's move to merge its operations stole the limelight.
Amplat's Lebowa Platinum Ltd finished up 110 cents at 440 cents following Amplats' announcement on Tuesday that all its operation would now be put in Rusplats.

The market which failed to take a cue from Wall Street's climb overnight was also buoyed by U.S. agency Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co's move to assign an investment grade BBB minus rating to the country's foreign currency obligations.
The industrial index ended up 3.3 points to 8,504.7, the gold index was down 12.8 points to 1,164.5 and the all-share index gained 20.6 points to 7,286.1.

Comments by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel that an interest rate cut was likely later this year had helped the market's financial index to close at another fresh high, although the rate cut news were now old news, dealers said.
The financial index ended up 45.5 points to 9,739.9.
Worries about the rand's recent slide on jitters about foreign exchange control relaxations were starting to dissipate.
The rand fell to 4.50 bid on the dollar on Monday -- its lowest level in four months -- but has since come back to hold steady around 4.49 bid.
Volumes on the day were high with 837 million rand worth of shares traded.
Dealers said gold shares were disappointing on the day as bullion remained dull, hovering in its recent $343-$344 range.
Dealers expected the overall market to hold around current levels on Thursday with the eyes focused on Wall Street's start by the local close.
In the broader market advancers just led decliners 187 to 182 and there were 29 news highs and 20 new lows.
